The perception categories that emerge from our model are brand image, familiarity/knowledge, long-term cost, norms/attitudes, policy/incentives, reliability/uncertainty, capital cost, suitability/compatibility, and sustainability. The synonyms that fall in each of these groups are shown in Appendix B to the peer reviewed publication. LDA implementation Referencing Equations above, the values of α, β, and k have a significant impact on the results of the model. Initially, we implemented a three-dimensional grid search to optimize parameter selection. After noticing inconsistent results between model runs, we searched for a solution using the ensemble LDA approach. Verification A key step in the development of this tool was the validation process. Two separate components required validation. First, the corpus itself was balanced with split-corpus validation testing to show that the resulting saliency scores were not a factor of a small portion of the papers. Next, the consistency of model results on the corrected corpus were verified. Split-corpus testing To check if there was similar influence from all members of the corpus, it was split into two different validation corpora. These were used to build separate LDA models. If there was a discrepancy in saliency scores for a term between the two models, this term was incorporated into a Google Scholar query with a uniform format. From here, the earliest results that are relevant to electric vehicle fleet adoption were added in equal parts to the two validation corpora and the process was repeated until the average difference in saliency scores for the targeted terms reached the pre-determined threshold. This is sometimes referred to as corpus augmentation. Model repeatability Typical LDA implementations sample from several random variables during Gibbs sampling, and therefore suffer from a lack of repeatability. To address this issue, we used the ensemble LDA (eLDA) routine, as implemented in Gensim69. eLDA uses density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise to categorize the number of topics and beta Dirichlet distributions that create stable results70.
